lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: Leave Horeb; leaders and judges appointed
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 1:1-18 opens Moses' words in the fortieth year: the LORD tells Israel to leave Horeb and take the land promised to the fathers, and Moses recalls appointing wise men as heads and judges who hear small and great alike without partiality.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell where and when Moses gave these speeches and what he told the judges?
ev: Say when and where Moses speaks (1:1-5).
Say what Moses charged the judges (1:16-17).

nodes.t: Moses recalls the spies and the refusal
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 1:19-46 has Moses recall the sending of twelve spies from Kadesh-barnea, Israel's refusal to go up despite the good fruit, the LORD's oath that that generation would not see the land except Caleb, and the failed attack when they presumed to go up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses reminded the new generation of the spies?
ev: Compare this retelling with Numbers 13-14 and name one thing Moses emphasizes (for example the LORD going before them, 1:30-33).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 2:1-23 recalls how the LORD told Israel not to fight Edom, Moab or Ammon because he had given them their land, how the generation of fighting men died during the thirty-eight years, and how the LORD had earlier given those lands to Esau's and Lot's descendants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel left Edom, Moab and Ammon alone?
ev: Say whose land Israel was told not to take and the reason given.
Say how long it took from Kadesh-barnea to the brook Zered (2:14).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 2:24-3:22 recalls the defeat of Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, the LORD hardening Sihon's spirit, the land east of the Jordan given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, and Moses' command that they cross armed with their brothers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Israel took the land east of the Jordan?
ev: Say who the two kings were and what happened to them.
Say what Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh must do before settling (3:18-20).

nodes.t: Moses may only see the land
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 3:23-29 records Moses pleading with the LORD to let him cross the Jordan, the LORD refusing for the people's sake and telling him to view the land from Pisgah and to charge and encourage Joshua.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses asked the LORD and the answer he received?
ev: Say what Moses asked and what the LORD answered.
Say what Moses was told to do for Joshua.

nodes.t: Hear the statutes: no images, remember Horeb
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 4:1-40 urges Israel to keep the statutes without adding or taking away, to remember the day at Horeb when they heard the voice from the fire and saw no form, to make no image, to beware of forgetting the covenant, and warns of exile yet promises that the LORD, merciful, will be found when sought.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses told Israel to make no image of God?
ev: Say what Israel saw and did not see at Horeb and why that rules out images (4:12, 15-19).
Find the promise about seeking the LORD from exile (4:29-31).

nodes.t: Three cities of refuge east of the Jordan
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 4:41-49 records Moses setting apart Bezer, Ramoth and Golan east of the Jordan for a slayer who killed without hatred to flee to, and introduces the law Moses sets before Israel in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the three cities east of the Jordan were for?
ev: Name the three cities and say who could flee there (4:42).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 5 has Moses remind Israel that the LORD made a covenant with them at Horeb, repeats the ten commandments given from the fire, and recounts the people's fear and Moses standing between them and the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the ten commandments and explain who gave them and to whom?
ev: Say the ten commandments in order.
Say what 5:2-3 says about whom the covenant was made with.
Find the reason attached to the sabbath commandment here (5:15).

nodes.t: Hear, O Israel: love the LORD
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 6 gives the great command to love the LORD with all heart, soul and might because he is one LORD, to teach the words to children throughout the day, to remember him when blessed in the land, and to answer a child's question with the story of the exodus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to love the LORD with all one's heart, soul and might?
ev: Say the command of 6:4-5 in your own words.
List the ways 6:6-9 says to keep the words before oneself and the children.

nodes.t: A holy people chosen in love
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 7 tells Israel to make no treaties or marriages with the nations of the land and to destroy their altars, because the LORD chose Israel not because they were many but because he loved them and keeps covenant with those who love him, and Israel is not to fear them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD chose Israel according to Deuteronomy 7:7-9?
ev: Say the reason 7:7-8 gives for why the LORD chose Israel.
Find the description of the LORD in 7:9.

nodes.t: Remember the wilderness; do not forget
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 8 calls Israel to remember how the LORD humbled and fed them with manna for forty years so they would learn that man lives by every word from the LORD's mouth, and warns against pride and forgetting him in the good land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses told Israel to remember the wilderness before they entered the land?
ev: Say what the manna was meant to teach (8:3).
Say what danger Moses warns about in 8:11-18.

nodes.t: Not for your righteousness: the calf recalled
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 9:1-10:11 has Moses tell Israel they will take the land not for their righteousness but for the nations' wickedness, recalling the golden calf, his breaking the tables and fasting forty days, his prayer for the people, and the second tables placed in the ark.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Moses used the golden calf to show Israel it did not earn the land?
ev: Say why Moses says Israel is not given the land for its righteousness (9:4-6).
Describe what Moses did after the calf and what the LORD wrote on the new tables (10:1-5).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 10:12-22 asks what the LORD requires: to fear him, walk in his ways, love and serve him with all the heart and keep his commandments; Israel is to circumcise the heart because the LORD of lords loves the stranger, orphan and widow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to circumcise the heart (10:16) in the context of this passage?
ev: List the things the LORD requires in 10:12-13.
Say what the LORD does for the fatherless, widow and stranger and what Israel is told in response (10:18-19).

nodes.t: Obey and be blessed; a blessing and a curse
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 11 calls Israel to love the LORD and remember his acts in Egypt and the wilderness, tells them the land is watered by the LORD's care, to bind his words upon them, and sets before them a blessing and a curse with mount Gerizim and mount Ebal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the choice that Moses set before Israel in Deuteronomy 11:26-28?
ev: Say how the land of promise differs from Egypt in its water (11:10-12).
Say what blessing and curse are set before Israel (11:26-28).

nodes.t: Worship at the place the LORD chooses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 12 tells Israel to destroy the pagan places of worship and to bring offerings, tithes and firstfruits to the one place the LORD will choose, rejoicing there with households and the Levite, while allowing ordinary meat to be eaten at home but not blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why chapter 12 sets worship at one place the LORD chooses?
ev: Say what Israel was to destroy and where they were to offer sacrifices.
Say what is allowed at home and what is still forbidden (12:15-16, 23-25).

nodes.t: Testing prophets and loyalty to the LORD
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 13 warns that a prophet or dreamer, a family member or a city that urges Israel to follow other gods must not be obeyed even if a sign comes true, because the LORD is testing Israel's love, and gives the penalties.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why a prophet whose sign came true was still not to be followed?
ev: Say how a prophet can give a sign and still be rejected (13:1-3).
Say what the chapter says to do with a city led astray (13:12-16).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 14 says Israel are children of the LORD and a holy people, so they are not to mutilate themselves for the dead, lists the clean and unclean animals, birds and fish, and gives the tithe to be eaten before the LORD, with a third-year tithe for the Levite, stranger, fatherless and widow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the third-year tithe was for?
ev: Say how this list compares with Leviticus 11 (the same kinds of marks).
Say who received the tithe of the third year (14:28-29).

nodes.t: The year of release and care for the poor
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 15 commands debts to be released every seventh year, tells Israel to lend freely to the poor and open the hand, to free Hebrew servants in the seventh year with a generous gift remembering Egypt, and to dedicate firstling animals to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Israel had to do for the poor and for a servant who had served six years?
ev: Say what happens every seventh year for debts and for servants.
Find the reason Moses gives for generosity (15:15).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 16 commands Passover, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles at the place the LORD chooses, with all males appearing three times a year and giving as they are able, and appoints just judges who take no bribes and forbids setting up images near the altar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the three feasts of Deuteronomy 16 and what judges had to avoid?
ev: Name the three feasts and the number of times males appear each year.
Say what the judges must not do (16:19).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 17:1-13 requires sacrifices without blemish, trial with at least two or three witnesses before a penalty for idolatry, and a place of final decision by priests and judge where hard cases are brought and whose sentence must be obeyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why two or three witnesses were needed before a person was put to death?
ev: Say how many witnesses were required (17:6).
Say where hard cases were to be taken.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 17:14-20 anticipates Israel asking for a king and says he must be one the LORD chooses from among their brothers, must not multiply horses, wives or silver, and must write a copy of the law and read it all his life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the king was to do with the law and what he was to avoid?
ev: List what the king must not multiply.
Say what the king must write and do with the law (17:18-19).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:1-8 says the Levites have no inheritance among their brothers because the LORD is their inheritance, lists the portions of sacrifices and firstfruits that are the priests' due, and allows a Levite from any town to serve at the chosen place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the Levites were provided for?
ev: Say what the Levites have instead of land.
Say what portions the priests were due.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:9-14 forbids Israel to learn the abominable practices of the nations: passing children through fire, divination, sorcery, charms, mediums and consulting the dead, which the LORD calls an abomination.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list practices Deuteronomy 18 forbids and say why?
ev: Name some of the practices forbidden here.
Say why the LORD is driving out the nations (18:12).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:15-22 promises that the LORD will raise up a prophet like Moses from among his brothers, recalls Israel's request at Horeb not to hear the LORD's voice directly, puts the LORD's words in the prophet's mouth, and gives a test for false prophets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised in Deuteronomy 18:15-19 and how to tell a false prophet?
ev: Say what the LORD promises in 18:15 and 18:18.
Give the test of 18:22 for a prophet who speaks in the LORD's name.

nodes.t: Cities of refuge and honest witnesses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 19 commands three cities of refuge in the land for accidental killers while the murderer who lies in wait is to be handed over, forbids moving a neighbour's landmark, and requires two or three witnesses, with the penalty of the false witness being what he intended for his brother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why a false witness received the punishment he planned for another?
ev: Say how an accidental killing differs from murder in this chapter.
Say what happens to a false witness (19:16-21).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 20 instructs that when Israel goes to battle the priest tells them not to fear since the LORD goes with them, certain men are excused from fighting, a distant city is offered peace first, the cities of the nations in the land are to be destroyed so Israel will not learn their abominations, and fruit trees are not to be cut down in a siege.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Israel was to do before attacking a far-off city and why the Canaanite cities were treated differently?
ev: Say what the priest says before battle (20:3-4).
Describe the offer of peace and the rule for trees.
Say the reason given for destroying the Canaanite cities (20:18).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 21:1-9 gives the rite when a slain man is found and the killer is unknown: the nearest city's elders break a heifer's neck in an unworked valley, wash their hands, declare innocence and ask the LORD not to lay innocent blood on Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the elders carried out the rite for an unsolved murder?
ev: Describe what the elders do and say.
Say why the rite is needed (21:8-9).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 21:10-23 gives rules about a captive woman taken as a wife, the firstborn right of the son of an unloved wife, the stubborn and rebellious son brought to the elders, and the burial before nightfall of a man hanged on a tree, who is accursed of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the rule about the firstborn of an unloved wife and the rule for a hanged man?
ev: Name the four situations in this section.
Say when a hanged man's body was to be buried and why (21:22-23).

nodes.t: Caring for a neighbour's property and the creation order
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 22:1-12 commands returning a brother's lost animals, helping a fallen ox, sparing the mother bird, putting a battlement on the roof, and various mixing laws (seeds, ox and ass, wool and linen) and tassels on garments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the text tells Israel to return a neighbour's lost animal and put a battlement on a roof?
ev: Give two commands in the section about helping a neighbour.
Say what the battlement was for (22:8).

nodes.t: Marriage, charge and sexual purity laws
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 22:13-30 treats a husband's false charge against his bride, adultery, a betrothed woman assaulted in the city or the field, a woman not betrothed, and a man's taking his father's wife, with penalties set out for each case.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how these laws protected a woman from false charges and from guilt for an assault she could not prevent?
ev: Say what the elders do in the case of a false charge (22:18-19).
Say how the text distinguishes the betrothed woman in the city from the field (22:23-27).

nodes.t: The congregation, the camp and a holy LORD among them
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 23:1-14 says who may not enter the congregation of the LORD (certain persons, Ammonites and Moabites to the tenth generation, with the Edomite and Egyptian treated differently), and commands the camp to be kept clean because the LORD walks in the midst of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD wanted the camp kept clean (23:14)?
ev: Say why Ammonites and Moabites were excluded (23:3-5).
Say why the camp must be kept clean (23:14).

nodes.t: Fugitive slaves, usury, vows and gleaning
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 23:15-25 forbids returning an escaped slave to his master, forbids prostitution in Israel and offering its wages, forbids interest on loans to a brother, calls for vows to be paid, and allows a neighbour to eat from a vineyard or field but not carry away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the text says about keeping a vow?
ev: Say what to do about an escaped servant (23:15-16).
Say what is allowed when passing a neighbour's vineyard.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 24:1-5 says a man who divorces his wife by a bill may not take her again after she has married another, and a newly married man is free from war for a year; 24:6-22 commands fair treatment of pledges, wages paid on the day, personal responsibility for sin, justice for stranger and orphan, and gleanings left for the poor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses tells Israel to remember Egypt when treating the poor and stranger?
ev: Say what the law of 24:1-4 forbids.
Say how Israel was to treat a poor man's pledge and wages (24:10-15).
Find the reason repeated in 24:18, 22.

nodes.t: Punishment limits, the ox and the brother's widow
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:1-12 limits a beating to forty stripes, forbids muzzling an ox that treads out the corn, gives the duty of a brother to raise up a name for a dead brother and the shoe-loosing ceremony if he refuses, and a rule about a wife seizing a man in a fight.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of the law of the brother's widow in 25:5-10?
ev: Say the limit on flogging and the reason (25:3).
Describe the duty of a living brother to a dead brother's childless widow.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:13-19 requires accurate weights and measures, calls dishonest dealing an abomination, and commands Israel to remember what Amalek did on the way from Egypt, attacking the weary, and blot out his memory when the LORD gives rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why honest weights and measures mattered to the LORD?
ev: Say what the LORD calls dishonest weights (25:16).
Say what Amalek did and what Israel is to do about it (25:17-19).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 26 commands a basket of firstfruits brought to the priest with a confession that tells Israel's story from a wandering Aramean father through Egypt to the gift of the land, a third-year tithe declaration, and a mutual avowal that the LORD is Israel's God and Israel his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Israel's story as the firstfruits confession tells it?
ev: Summarize the confession said with the firstfruits (26:5-10).
Say what Israel and the LORD each avouch in 26:17-19.

nodes.t: Stones, altar and the curses from Ebal
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 27 commands that on crossing the Jordan Israel set up stones with the law written on them and an altar on mount Ebal, and that tribes stand on Gerizim to bless and Ebal to curse, with Levites declaring twelve curses to each of which all the people say Amen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Israel was to do at Gerizim and Ebal?
ev: Say which tribes stood on which mount.
Name several of the sins cursed and what the people answer (27:15-26).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 28:1-14 promises that if Israel hearkens diligently to the LORD, blessings will overtake them in city and field, in children, crops and herds, victory over enemies, plenty of rain and being the head not the tail, if they do not turn aside.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised Israel if they obeyed?
ev: List areas of life that are blessed (28:3-6).
State the condition repeated in 28:1, 9, 13-14.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 28:15-68 sets out the curses that will come if Israel does not obey: sickness, drought, defeat, siege, exile among the nations and a return to Egypt, because they did not serve the LORD joyfully for all he gave.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare the blessings of verses 1-14 with the curses that follow?
ev: Say why the text says these curses come (28:47).
Describe the final picture of exile in 28:64-68.

nodes.t: The covenant in the land of Moab
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 29 calls Israel, including children and strangers, to enter the LORD's covenant and oath that day, warns that anyone who turns to idols will bear the curses of this covenant, and says the nations will ask why the land is ruined, to be answered that they forsook the covenant; the secret things belong to the LORD and the revealed things to Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what covenant Israel enters in Deuteronomy 29 and what happens if they forsake it?
ev: Say who stands in the covenant ceremony (29:10-15).
Say what the nations will be told about a ruined land (29:24-28).
Find 29:29 and say what it says belongs to the LORD and what to Israel.

nodes.t: Return to the LORD; the word is near; choose life
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 30 says that when blessing and curse have come and Israel returns and obeys, the LORD will gather them, bring them to the land, and circumcise their hearts; the commandment is not hidden or far off but very near, and Moses sets life and death before them and calls them to choose life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the choice set before Israel in Deuteronomy 30:15-20?
ev: Say what the LORD promises when Israel returns (30:1-6).
Say what 30:11-14 says about where the word is.
Say the choice in 30:19.

nodes.t: Joshua commissioned; the law read every seven years
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 31 records Moses at 120 years old encouraging Israel and Joshua that the LORD goes before them and will not fail them, writing the law and giving it to the priests to read every seventh year, the LORD predicting Israel's turning away, and the book of the law placed beside the ark.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses told Israel to do with the law after his death?
ev: Say what Moses told Joshua (31:7-8).
Say when and to whom the law is to be read (31:10-13).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 32:1-43 is a song that praises the LORD as the Rock whose work is perfect, recalls his care for Jacob in the wilderness, accuses Israel of forgetting him and worshipping other gods, tells of judgment, yet says vengeance is the LORD's and he will judge his people and be merciful to his land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize the song in three parts: the LORD's faithfulness, Israel's unfaithfulness and the LORD's judgment and mercy?
ev: Describe the picture of the LORD as the Rock in 32:3-4.
Summarize what Israel did in return for his care (32:15-18).

nodes.t: Moses is told to go up Nebo
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 32:44-52 records Moses speaking the song with Joshua, telling Israel to set their hearts on the words because they are their life, and the LORD telling him to go up mount Nebo to see the land and die because of the trespass at Meribah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD told Moses to go up Nebo?
ev: Say why Moses is told he will not enter the land (32:51).
Say what Moses tells Israel about the words of the law (32:46-47).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 33 records Moses' blessing of Israel before his death: the LORD coming from Sinai, a blessing in turn on Reuben, Judah, Levi, Benjamin, Joseph, Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali and Asher, and a close praising the LORD as Israel's refuge and shield.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say something Moses blessed about two of the tribes and how the chapter ends?
ev: Name the tribes blessed.
Find the closing description of the LORD in 33:26-29.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 34 tells how Moses goes up Nebo and sees the whole land the LORD swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, dies at 120 and is buried by the LORD in Moab, Israel mourns thirty days, Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom, and no prophet since has been like Moses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Moses' life ended and who led Israel next?
ev: Say what the LORD showed Moses and said to him (34:1-4).
Say how the chapter describes Moses and who takes his place (34:9-12).

nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.d: After forty days of fasting Jesus is tempted three times by the devil and answers each with “it is written”; the devil leaves and angels minister to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the devil offered Jesus and how Jesus replied?
ev: List the three temptations
Say what Jesus answered each time

nodes.t: Divorce, oaths, retaliation and love for enemies
nodes.d: Jesus teaches on divorce, on plain speech instead of oaths, on not resisting evil with evil, and on loving and praying for enemies, as the Father gives sun and rain to evil and good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about loving enemies and why?
ev: Say what Jesus teaches about oaths (5:33-37)
Explain the command about enemies and the reason given in 5:45

nodes.d: Tested by Pharisees, Jesus points back to male and female at the beginning and “one flesh”, says what God joined man must not separate, speaks of Moses’ allowance because of hard hearts, and says not all can receive the saying about eunuchs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about marriage and why?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from the beginning
Explain why Moses allowed divorce according to 19:8

nodes.d: Sadducees pose a puzzle about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that in the resurrection they are as angels, and that God is God of the living.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees denied
Explain how Jesus uses the words about Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

nodes.d: Asked which is the great commandment, Jesus answers love the Lord with all heart, soul and mind, and love your neighbour as yourself, and says all the law and the prophets hang on these two.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the two great commandments and what they cover?
ev: State the two commandments
Explain “on these two hang all the law and the prophets”

nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: Marriage and divorce, and blessing the children
nodes.d: Tested about divorce, Jesus points to creation: male and female, leaving father and mother and becoming one flesh; later he welcomes children, saying the kingdom of God belongs to such and must be received as a child.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught about marriage and about children?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from creation about marriage
Explain what he says about the children

nodes.d: Sadducees who deny the resurrection ask about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that the risen are as angels, and that God is God of the living, citing the bush.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees asked
Explain Jesus’ use of the words from the bush

nodes.d: A scribe asks which commandment is first; Jesus answers the Lord is one and to love him with all heart, soul, mind and strength, and second to love your neighbour as yourself; the scribe agrees and Jesus says he is not far from the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the two great commandments?
ev: State the two commandments
Say what the scribe added and what Jesus replied

nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.d: Full of the Spirit, Jesus is tempted forty days by the devil and answers each of three temptations with 'It is written' and a word of Scripture; the devil departs for a season.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the three temptations and how Jesus answered them?
ev: Name the three temptations and how Jesus answered each.

nodes.d: Asked by a lawyer what he must do to inherit eternal life, Jesus draws out love of God and neighbour; to the question 'who is my neighbour' he tells of a Samaritan who helps a man left by robbers after a priest and a Levite pass by.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the good Samaritan and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do?
ev: Retell the parable and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do.

nodes.t: The Sadducees Ask About the Resurrection
nodes.d: The Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, ask whose wife a woman married to seven brothers would be; Jesus says those counted worthy of that world neither marry nor die, and the dead are raised, as Moses called the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' answer to the Sadducees about the resurrection?
ev: Say what Jesus said about the resurrection and how he used Moses.

nodes.t: I Am the Light of the World
nodes.d: Jesus says 'I am the light of the world', that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness, and defends his testimony as true because the Father who sent him also bears witness; he says those who do not believe that he is he will die in their sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 'I am the light of the world' and what Jesus warns those who do not believe?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself as light and what he says to those who do not believe.

nodes.d: Peter tells the amazed crowd that the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up, and that faith in his name made the man strong. He calls them to repent so that their sins may be blotted out, and reminds them of God's covenant with the fathers and the blessing promised to Abraham's seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said made the man walk and what he urged the crowd to do?
ev: Say whom Peter credits for the healing (3:12-16)
Explain what Peter calls the people to do and why (3:18-19, 3:25-26)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Moses and the people's refusal
nodes.d: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, the birth and upbringing of Moses, his first attempt to help his brethren and their rejection, and God's call from the burning bush. He says the people refused Moses, turned back in their hearts to Egypt, and made a calf.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen says Israel treated Moses, whom God sent as ruler and deliverer?
ev: Retell the stages of Moses' life Stephen names (7:20-36)
Say how Stephen says the fathers treated Moses (7:35, 7:39-41)

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.d: Paul explains the law's relationship to sin and describes the struggle with sin in the one who delights in God's law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Paul says the law is good for and what it cannot do (Romans 7)?
ev: Explain 7:12
Describe the struggle in 7:15-25

nodes.d: Righteousness is for everyone who believes; faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 10:9-10 and 10:17?
ev: State 10:9-10
Explain 10:17

nodes.d: In view of God's mercies, believers present their bodies as a living sacrifice, are transformed by the renewing of the mind, and live in love as members of one body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 12:1-2?
ev: Explain 12:1-2
List ways Paul describes love in practice (12:9-21)

nodes.d: Paul teaches submission to governing authorities as God's servants, and sums up the law in love for neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 13:1-7 teaches?
ev: State what Paul says about authorities (13:1-7)
Explain 13:8-10

nodes.d: Believers are to welcome one another, not judge over disputable matters, and seek the good of their neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says to treat a brother who disagrees on disputable matters?
ev: Explain 14:1 and 14:17

nodes.t: Paul's rights given up for the gospel
nodes.d: Paul defends his apostleship and his right to be supported, but says he has not used that right, becoming all things to all people so that he might save some.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul gave up his rights, using 1 Corinthians 9:19-23?
ev: List the rights Paul says he has (9:4-6)
Explain why he did not use them (9:12, 9:18)
Explain what Paul means by becoming all things to all men (9:19-22)

nodes.d: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, who were turning to another gospel, to defend justification by faith, the freedom of the sons of God and life by the Spirit (1:1-6:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul wrote to the Galatians and what he says the true gospel is?
ev: Say what problem prompted the letter (1:6-9)
Name the three parts: Paul's defence (1-2), justification by faith (3-4), living by the Spirit (5-6)

nodes.t: Abraham, faith and the blessing for the nations
nodes.d: Paul argues that Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness, so those of faith are Abraham's children, and that Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Galatians 3:6-9 connects Abraham's faith to the Gentiles?
ev: Quote what Paul says Abraham did (3:6)
Explain who are the children of Abraham (3:7)
Say what the scripture foresaw (3:8)
Explain how Christ redeemed us from the curse (3:13-14)

nodes.t: Honouring widows and caring for family
nodes.d: Timothy is to treat people of every age with respect, honour widows who are truly widows, expect families to care for their own, and set guidelines for enrolling widows and for younger widows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is to care for widows according to 5:4 and 5:16?
ev: State what 5:8 says about providing for one's own
Describe the tasks of a widow indeed (5:5, 5:10)

nodes.d: Paul's letter to Timothy at Ephesus about sound doctrine, prayer, order in the church, qualified leaders, and a minister's conduct and charge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Timothy is about (see 3:14-15)?
ev: Describe how 3:15 states the letter's purpose
Name the main sections: false teaching, prayer and conduct, leaders, Timothy's ministry, groups in the church, closing charge

nodes.t: Warning against wilful sin; endure and live by faith
nodes.d: The writer warns that no sacrifice remains for wilful sin after receiving the truth, reminds readers of their earlier endurance, and urges patience, since the just shall live by faith and they are not of those who draw back.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer asks the readers to remember and do in 10:32-39?
ev: Describe the warning of 10:26-29
State what the just shall do (10:38)
Tell what the readers endured before (10:32-34)

nodes.t: Not Mount Sinai but Mount Zion
nodes.d: Believers have not come to the fearful mountain of Sinai but to mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, to God, to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant and to the blood of sprinkling; they must not refuse the one who speaks, and receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hebrews 12:18-24 contrasts Sinai with Zion and names Jesus there?
ev: Contrast the two mountains (12:18-24)
State what is said of the kingdom and of God (12:28-29)

nodes.d: The writer calls for brotherly love and hospitality to strangers, remembering prisoners, honour in marriage, and a life free from covetousness because God has said he will never leave or forsake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some practical commands in 13:1-5 and the promise that supports them?
ev: List the commands of 13:1-5
Say what promise supports contentment (13:5)

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.t: Epilogue: I come quickly, the invitation and the warning
nodes.d: The angel and Jesus confirm the words are faithful and true, Jesus says he comes quickly with his reward and is the Alpha and Omega and the bright and morning star, the Spirit and the bride say Come and invite the thirsty, a warning is given about adding to or taking from the book, and the book ends with the grace of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Revelation ends and what invitation it gives?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself in 22:12-16
Quote the invitation of 22:17 in your own words
Say what the warning in 22:18-19 is about
